title: Getting Started
subtitle: Bloom's skill tabs, the controls, and getting around.

quests.title: Your Quest Book
quests.subtitle: Start here
description: This book suggests things to try. Nothing in it is locked, so pick any quest in any order.
Open it with the book button at the top-left of your inventory, or give "Open Quests" a key in Controls.
Lines show a good order: what usually comes first. Do a quest early and it gets a grey tick; it pays out once the quests before it are done.
Click a checkmark task to tick it, then click a reward to claim it. Your progress is your own.
Ctrl+K opens Keybind Atlas: a map of your keyboard and mouse showing what each key does in this pack.

quests.title: Recipes and Labels
description: JEI lists every item beside your inventory. Search for one, or hover over any item and press R to see how it's made, U to see what it's used for.
Jade's small panel at the top of the screen names the block or creature you're looking at, and the mod it comes from.

quests.title: Roll and Swing
description: Press Z to dodge roll the way you're moving. Nothing can hit you mid-roll, and it's ready again after about 3 seconds. You can't roll in the air or when you're low on food.
Better Combat gives every weapon its own swings. Keep attacking, or hold the button, for a combo; one swing can hit several mobs.
Two-Handed weapons (the tooltip says so) ignore your off hand. With a one-handed weapon in each hand, your swings alternate between them.

quests.title: Carry On
description: With both hands empty, hold Shift and right-click a chest, barrel or furnace to pick it up with everything inside. Right-click a spot to set it down.
Most animals can be carried the same way, but not monsters. Heavy things slow you down.

quests.title: The Skill Hub
quests.subtitle: The heart of the pack
description: Bloom gives you four skill tabs, Combat, Armor, Utility and Misc, each levelling from 0 to 100 through its own kind of play.
Open the Skill Hub with its button in the column along the left side of your inventory, or give "Open Skill Hub" a key in Controls.
Each level is one stat point for that tab: spend it with the + beside a stat on the left. Click a stat's icon to switch it off or on.
Points stay where you put them until that tab reaches level 100, so choose with some care. This quest's reward is one level in every tab.

quests.title: Majors
description: Majors are the big abilities: weapon tricks, new defenses, odd rules, even flight. They cost Major Levels, not stat points.
You get one Major Level for every 10 levels in any tab, and can spend it in any tab. The strip under the page shows how many are free.
Click a Major to buy it, click it again to switch it off or on, and right-click an owned one for its details. A locked one only says Prerequisite Required.
Single Majors can't be refunded: a tab's white arrows (top right) refund all of its Majors, then need 20 minutes before the next time.

quests.title: Spend Your XP
description: Under a tab's stats, the "+1 level" button buys that tab its next level with vanilla XP. It never takes more than the level needs.
It's a way to raise a tab you rarely play. Here are a few levels to try it with.
At level 100 it becomes "Buy point": extra stat points that stay yours for good.

quests.title: Pocket and Runes
description: Two Misc Majors open screens of their own, from the chest and enchanted book buttons under the Skill Hub button (or /bloom pocket and /bloom runes, or a key of your own in Controls).
Hoarder's Pocket (5 Major Levels): nine slots that keep their items through death. No shulker boxes or bundles.
Rune Embedding (6 Major Levels): five slots for enchanted books. Slots 1-4 work while you wear no armor, slot 5 while your main hand is empty. The books aren't used up.

quests.title: The Combat Tab
quests.subtitle: XP from fighting
description: Combat XP comes from the damage you deal to mobs, with a bonus for the killing blow.
Stats: Power (damage), Tempo (attack speed), Critical (harder crits), Penetration (ignore armor) and Looting (better drops).
Majors grow from six weapon trees (sword, axe, bow, crossbow, trident, bare hands) plus a row for any weapon. The pack's spears and daggers count as swords, its maces and hammers as axes.
Majors that need a key use Weapon skill, on V.

quests.title: The Armor Tab
quests.subtitle: XP from taking hits
description: Armor XP comes from damage you take, with extra for hits you block with a shield or avoid with Dodge.
Stats: Vitality (more hearts), Defense (armor of your own), Dodge (a chance to avoid a hit) and Durability (armor and shields wear slower).
Each armor piece is Light (leather, chainmail, robes), Medium (iron, gold, copper) or Heavy (diamond, netherite, full knight's plate).
With the Fitting Armor Major (2 Major Levels), a full set gives its bonus: Light dodges more and falls softer, Medium and Heavy take less damage.

quests.title: The Utility Tab
quests.subtitle: XP from gathering
description: Utility XP comes from mining, chopping, digging, harvesting ripe crops, fishing and shearing. Ores are worth the most.
Use the right tool for the block; blocks you placed yourself give nothing.
Stats: Efficiency (faster tool work), Yield (extra drops from ores, logs and crops) and Preservation (tools wear slower).
Its Majors include Vein Mining and Timber, which take a whole ore vein or tree at once. Sneak to break just the one block.

quests.title: The Misc Tab
quests.subtitle: XP from experience orbs
description: Misc XP comes from the experience orbs you pick up, and you still get all of their vanilla XP.
Stats: Wisdom (more XP from orbs), Speed (move faster) and Endurance (food lasts longer).
Its Majors are the strange ones: safer food, effects that last, more storage, even flight (Ascension, 20 Major Levels).

quests.title: Maps
description: The round minimap keeps north at the top. Hostile mobs show red, animals green, neutral mobs yellow and your own pets sky blue.
Press M for the world map, B to save a waypoint where you stand, and Y for the minimap's settings.
When you die, the map marks the spot as Latest Death.
The reward is what a Warp Stone takes (see Waystones).

quests.title: Waystones
description: Waystones stand in many villages and here and there in the wild. Right-click one to activate it; after that, right-click any waystone to travel to the others you've activated.
A Warp Stone (4 amethyst shards, 4 ender pearls and an emerald) opens the same list anywhere: hold right-click. It needs 30 seconds between uses.
Or craft it with 3 stone bricks and 3 obsidian into a waystone of your own, for your base.

quests.title: After a Death
description: When you die, your body stays where you fell with all your items on it. It won't burn in lava or fall into the void, and it waits for you.
Right-click it and press Transfer Items to put everything back where it was. An empty body disappears; after an hour a full one turns to a skeleton, still holding everything.
Anyone can open it, so friends can bring your things back for you.

quests.title: Loot for Everyone
description: Chests, barrels and chest minecarts that come with the world hold a separate share of loot for every player.
If a friend looted one first, your share is still waiting, so there's no need to race each other.
